# Data Integrity Requirements Quality Checklist: In-Browser Indexing

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is the publication boundary specific enough to prevent a falsely complete index after cancellation, worker failure, quota failure, migration failure, or database write failure? [Clarity, Spec §FR-038]
- [x] CHK007 Is manual refresh specified with deterministic relative-path and content-hash comparison rather than timestamp-only freshness? [Clarity, Spec §FR-040, Codebase §src/extraction/index.ts]
- [x] CHK008 Are recoverable per-file errors bounded with aggregate counts, at most 100 file details, and a truncation flag? [Clarity, Spec §FR-040]
- [x] CHK009 Are worker RPC terminal states specified as exactly one complete, cancelled, failed, or partial-warning state? [Clarity, Spec §FR-041, Contract §Progress Events]
- [x] CHK010 Are exact delete data classes named without implying writes to the user's source folder? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029, Spec §FR-036, Data Model §Data Retention]

- [x] CHK027 Are existing CodeGraph DB conventions for migration transactions, file-bundle writes, delete boundaries, and vector model metadata used as requirements-writing precedent? [Dependency, Codebase §src/db/schema.sql, Codebase §src/db/migrations.ts, Codebase §src/db/queries.ts]
- [x] CHK028 Are browser capability failures required to report stable error codes instead of corrupting repository state? [Dependency, Data Model §Error Taxonomy, Contract §Failure Handling]

## Research Notes

- SQLite-Wasm SAH-pool evidence supports one active owner, worker-held SQLite access, no COOP/COEP requirement, and explicit close/pause behavior before handoff.
- Web Locks evidence supports origin-scoped lock ownership that releases at callback completion and is available in workers.
- Current CodeGraph evidence shows schema versioning through `schema_versions`, migration transactions with `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, file delete transactions, and vector rows keyed by model, dimensions, BLOB, and input hash.
